content.comment_body: I developed a program in FBD using [product_name] V8 with 318 function blocks and a layout memory of 79867 bytes. The simulation was successful. Afterwards, I installed [product_name] V8.2, opened the program, and once again simulated it without issues. However, when I attempted to upload this program from my PC to a [product_name] 8 device, FS 06, via [product_name] V8.2, I encountered an error shown in the info window: [product_name] 8.FS4 Download failed, and the program could not be uploaded to the device. I realize my layout memory exceeds 30000 bytes, which causes program lines to mix after upload, but I’m still unclear why the program can’t be downloaded onto the device.
Would you be able to upload your program file?
As mentioned earlier, when I try to upload the program from the PC to the [product_name] device, the error occurs and the upload fails.
I meant uploading it to the forum as a ZIP file, not to the [product_name] device.

There seems to be an issue with the file. The information window in [product_name] does not provide specifics, only stating that the transmission failed, with no further details. In your situation, I would suggest submitting a support request to [company_name] for a detailed examination of the file.
Please remove the 'Asynchronous pulse generator' between M28 and Q12 and insert a new one.

Thank you very much—your suggestion was extremely helpful, and the program was successfully downloaded to the [product_name] device. Could you explain how you identified this error, especially since there was no error message in [product_name]? Did you use a specific tool or manually check the program line by line?

Here's one way to check: In the menu under Edit > Block Properties (All Blocks), you'll find a list of all blocks along with their properties. You can scroll through to spot any irregularities, such as a block missing a number. If you use the 'Select block from drawing' option, the chosen block will be directly displayed in the diagram.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced failure when attempting to transfer a large project created in [product_name] V8.2 to a [product_name] 8 FS 06 device. While simulation succeeded, the actual hardware transfer did not, with only a vague failure message and no detailed diagnostics. The underlying issue was a problematic 'asynchronous pulse generator' block, which needed to be deleted and replaced for the upload to succeed. This highlights the lack of specific error feedback in [product_name] and shows how faulty blocks can prevent successful downloads.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable transfers of simulated programs from their PC to [product_name] hardware and desire precise diagnostic messages when problems occur.
